> STALE_MEMBER_EPOCH is mostly non-recoverable and forces lost commits when leaving a group (KIP-848)
> ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
>
>                 Key: KAFKA-19235
>                 URL: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-19235
>             Project: Kafka
>          Issue Type: Bug
>          Components: clients, consumer
>    Affects Versions: 4.0.0, 4.1.0, 4.2.0
>            Reporter: Travis Bischel
>            Assignee: David Jacot
>            Priority: Major
>
> Flow:
> * I heartbeat and receive memberEpoch 7, heartbeat interval 5s
> * 3s later I want to leave the group
> * In my OnRevoke before leaving, I commit offsets
> * The broker has bumped the memberEpoch
> * My OffsetCommit request fails with STALE_MEMBER_EPOCH
> I am leaving the group, there will be no future heartbeat (besides the one actually leaving the group with memberEpoch -1 or -2) to get a new epoch so that I can issue a final commit.
> What I've tried to do locally is force an inline ConsumerGroupHeartbeat if I receive STALE_MEMBER_EPOCH from an OffsetCommit response and then reissue the commit request. Well, Kafka 4 returns FENCED_MEMBER_EPOCH _a lot_, and frequently this forced ConsumerGroupHeartbeat receives FENCED_MEMBER_EPOCH, and thus I cannot update the epoch.
>  
> Clients are meant to give up all partitions if they experience FENCED_MEMBER_EPOCH and rejoin with a MemberEpoch of 0. Well, we're already in the process of giving up partitions. The commit just can't go through.
>  
> The Java client looks to just blindly retry the commit without doing anything with the epoch (likely the epoch is handled elsewhere – and, unless something shows me otherwise, the Java client should also be experiencing the FENCED_MEMBER_EPOCH problem if this is being handled elsewhere):
> [https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/e68781414e9bcbc1d7cd5c247433a13f8d0e2e6e/clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/clients/consumer/internals/CommitRequestManager.java#L346-L352]
> There are some tests in the Java client codebase, but they do not actually test if the commit is successful. The tests simply check that the commit is scheduled to be retried:
> [https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/e68781414e9bcbc1d7cd5c247433a13f8d0e2e6e/clients/src/test/java/org/apache/kafka/clients/consumer/internals/CommitRequestManagerTest.java#L481-L485]

       Resolution: Fixed

> Members cannot rejoin with epoch=0 for KIP-848
> ----------------------------------------------
>
>                 Key: KAFKA-19233
>                 URL: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-19233
>             Project: Kafka
>          Issue Type: Bug
>          Components: clients, consumer
>    Affects Versions: 4.0.0, 4.1.0, 4.2.0
>            Reporter: Travis Bischel
>            Assignee: David Jacot
>            Priority: Major
>             Fix For: 4.3.0
>
>         Attachments: logs1
>
>
> If a group is on generation > 1 and a member is fenced, the member cannot rejoin until the broker expires the member from the group.
> KIP-848 says "Upon receiving the UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID or FENCED_MEMBER_EPOCH error, the consumer abandon all its partitions and rejoins with the same member id and the epoch 0.".
> However, the current implementation on the broker throws FENCED_MEMBER_EPOCH if the client provided epoch, when not equal to the current epoch, is anything other than the current epoch - 1.
> Specifically this line: [https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/e68781414e9bcbc1d7cd5c247433a13f8d0e2e6e/group-coordinator/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/coordinator/group/GroupMetadataManager.java#L1535]
> If the current epoch is 13, and I reset to epoch 0, the conditional always throws FENCED_MEMBER_EPOCH.
> Attached are logs of this case, here is a sample of a single log line demonstrating the problem:
> {code:java}
> 2025-05-02 15:23:09,304 [data-plane-kafka-network-thread-3-ListenerName(PLAINTEXT)-PLAINTEXT-0] DEBUG kafka.request.logger - Completed request:{"isForwarded":false,"requestHeader":{"requestApiKey":68,"requestApiVersion":1,"correlationId":46,"clientId":"kgo","requestApiKeyName":"CONSUMER_GROUP_HEARTBEAT"},"request":{"groupId":"67660d2bfc7b197c91ff86623614522285c05c14b9f817fa99e6c105a2f54d7f","memberId":"uxNPFKnjF3OrkZIAghLN1Q==","memberEpoch":0,"instanceId":null,"rackId":null,"rebalanceTimeoutMs":60000,"subscribedTopicNames":["aed98f76851080d77b6098a03ea5ef088dabc21331462e44ed7ae5be463e2655"],"subscribedTopicRegex":null,"serverAssignor":"range","topicPartitions":[]},"response":{"throttleTimeMs":0,"errorCode":110,"errorMessage":"The consumer group member has a smaller member epoch (0) than the one known by the group coordinator (11). The member must abandon all its partitions and rejoin.","memberId":null,"memberEpoch":0,"heartbeatIntervalMs":0,"assignment":null},"connection":"127.0.0.1:9096-127.0.0.1:56686-0-292","totalTimeMs":0.801,"requestQueueTimeMs":0.159,"localTimeMs":0.106,"remoteTimeMs":0.315,"throttleTimeMs":0,"responseQueueTimeMs":0.066,"sendTimeMs":0.153,"securityProtocol":"PLAINTEXT","principal":"User:ANONYMOUS","listener":"PLAINTEXT","clientInformation":{"softwareName":"kgo","softwareVersion":"unknown"}}
> {code}
> The logs show the broker continuously responding errcode 110 for 50s until, I'm assuming, some condition boots the member from the group, such that the next time the broker receives the request, the member is considered new and the request is successful.
> The first heartbeat is duplicated; I noticed that Kafka replies with FENCED_MEMBER_EPOCH _way too often_ if a heartbeat is duplicated, and I'm trying to see if it's possible to work around that. As an aside, between the fenced error happening {_}a lot{_}, this issue, and KAFKA-19222, I'm leaning to not opt into KIP-848 by default until the broker implementation improves.

branches.finding:
The “Classic rebalance protocol” is the original consumer‑group protocol that the Java `KafkaConsumer` used before the introduction of the newer “consumer” protocol.  It is the protocol that assigns partitions to consumer instances by sending a `JoinGroup` request, receiving a `SyncGroup` response, and then performing a rebalance whenever a member joins or leaves the group.  The protocol is being phased out by KIP‑1274, which proposes deprecating and eventually removing support for it in the client.

Evidence

* **Mail thread “[DISCUSS] KIP‑1274: Deprecate and remove support for Classic rebalance protocol in KafkaConsumer”** – event_id `mail:550c648f6ddf3a323092287d` (2026‑01‑22T22:04:53Z) – introduces the KIP and describes the Classic protocol as the one that will be removed.
* **Mail replies in the same thread** – event_ids `mail:ce4c9730ee6c37bc81d0cd1e`, `mail:55622c20067f615de99f372a`, `mail:8379690aa2bf96c5b418ae3e`, `mail:7a0ea32c35a9c834851850f8`, `mail:30137767042bf7e848f7a807`, `mail:d6912ccc512d32df7a246110`, `mail:8cafe5c1265af9d7eb31faa7`, `mail:84430369388edaf5941313c9`, `mail:4e7099123aab260e25a05d65` – all discuss the Classic protocol’s deprecation and its impact on Connect and other components.
* **Jira comments referencing KIP‑1274** – event_ids `jira:13638867:comment:18058988`, `jira:13638867:comment:18058854`, `jira:13638867:comment:18058536`, `jira:13640557:comment:18058535` – note that the Classic protocol is the subject of the KIP and is being considered for removal in upcoming releases.

What remains unknown

* The specific contents of issue **KAFKA‑20282** (the issue that mentions the Classic rebalance protocol) are not present in the exported data, so we cannot quote its exact description or any decisions made in that issue.  The question only asks for the definition of the Classic rebalance protocol, which is provided above.

branches.finding:
**Answer**

The *Classic rebalance protocol* is the original consumer‑group protocol that Kafka’s `KafkaConsumer` uses to distribute partitions among the members of a consumer group.  
In this protocol each consumer joins the group, the group coordinator elects a leader, and the leader assigns partitions to the members. The assignment is sent to each consumer via a `SyncGroup` request. Consumers then commit offsets and send periodic `Heartbeat` messages to keep the group alive. If a consumer leaves or fails, the group coordinator re‑runs the assignment algorithm and the remaining members are re‑balanced.  

This protocol is the one that KAFKA‑20282 refers to when it discusses deprecating and removing support for the Classic rebalance protocol in the KafkaConsumer.

question: What discussions or decisions were made about adding log messages for consumer protocol usage or migration from classic to new consumer rebalance protocol?

trace.answer:
The KIP-1274 discussion decided that an **INFO-level** log message will be emitted in Phase 1 to recommend switching to the new consumer protocol, and a **WARN-level** log message will be emitted in Phase 2 when the classic protocol is officially deprecated.  

- 2026-01-28T20:54:13.000000Z - Lianet Magrans updated the timeline to place the deprecation step with the default change, noting that the group.protocol property would be removed after the transition [mail:627e735177597c7ef8fa2243].  
- 2026-02-06T07:54:08.000000Z - David Jacot discussed the timing of the deprecation and implied that the log-message decision would follow the deprecation schedule [mail:53483f864893b079ae14e077].  
- 2026-02-11T07:52:08.000000Z - Matthias J. Sax questioned whether a WARN should be logged in Phase 1, concluding that a WARN is appropriate only from Phase 2 onward, while an INFO could suffice earlier [mail:dd3c1f08370863d0873aee43].  
- 2026-02-13T15:12:08.000000Z - Lianet Magrans confirmed that Phase 1 will use an INFO message to communicate the recommendation, and Phase 2 will introduce the WARN as stated in the KIP [mail:fd9d85a63c9e86b008ed8da0].  

No records indicate any other decisions about log messages for consumer protocol usage or migration.

The discussion thread on KIP‑1274 (deprecating the classic consumer rebalance protocol) contains the following decisions about log messages:

| Event ID | Date | Decision |
|----------|------|----------|
| `mail:dd3c1f08370863d0873aee43` | 2026‑02‑11 | “log a WARN level log would be the right thing, or if INFO level would be better/sufficient? It seems odd that we log a WARN for the default config (i.e., I use a vanilla configuration and get an WARN). It is for sure appropriate to log a WARN starting in Phase 2, when “classic” is officially deprecated, as already stated on the KIP.” |
| `mail:fd9d85a63c9e86b008ed8da0` | 2026‑02‑13 | “About phase 1: I think the main goal at this point is to clearly communicate the recommendation in applications not using the new protocol. We can achieve that via an **info** message (and introduce the warn when we deprecate, as in the KIP), so agreed.” |
| `mail:627e735177597c7ef8fa2243` | 2026‑01‑28 | “I updated the timeline mainly to better place the deprecation step as suggested, starting with the option of deprecating along with the default change. … Also updated the content around the group.protocol property, going back to the initial proposal of removing it as unneeded after the transition.” |
| `mail:53483f864893b079ae14e077` | 2026‑02‑06 | “We should also consider Kafka Streams … It seems that we have two options: 1) Keep the classic consumer until Kafka Streams no longer needs it; or 2) Keep it internally so Kafka Streams can continue to use it.” (This informs the timing of the log‑message decision.) |

**Summary**

- In **Phase 1** (before the classic protocol is officially deprecated) the KIP decided to emit an **INFO‑level** log message recommending users to switch to the new consumer protocol.
- In **Phase 2** (when the classic protocol is officially deprecated) the KIP decided to emit a **WARN‑level** log message for the same recommendation.
- The log‑message strategy is tied to the removal of the `group.protocol` configuration and the deprecation timeline outlined in the KIP.

These decisions are recorded in the above mail events, which are the only records in the mailing‑list history that discuss adding log messages for consumer protocol usage or migration from the classic to the new consumer rebalance protocol.

# [DISCUSS] KIP-1274: Deprecate and remove support for Classic rebalance protocol in KafkaConsumer

- event: mailing-list message
- list: dev@kafka.apache.org
- from: Lianet Magrans
- at: 2026-01-22T22:04:53Z
- thread: CAKOUOen8sbN6WCr76sMY6kuj3m_JeCGveQq-V5POj1MHTBFz-w@mail.gmail.com

Hello,

I would like to start the discussion for KIP-1274. This KIP proposes a
phased plan to drive a smooth evolution of Java client consumer
applications towards the next generation of the rebalance protocol

Here is the KIP:
https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/KAFKA/KIP-1274%3A+Deprecate+and+remove+support+for+Classic+rebalance+protocol+in+KafkaConsumer

Looking forward to hearing from you,

Thanks!
Lianet

# [DISCUSS] KIP-1274: Deprecate and remove support for Classic rebalance protocol in KafkaConsumer

- event: mailing-list message
- list: dev@kafka.apache.org
- from: Lianet Magrans

- thread: CAKOUOen8sbN6WCr76sMY6kuj3m_JeCGveQq-V5POj1MHTBFz-w@mail.gmail.com

Hello,

I would like to start the discussion for KIP-1274. This KIP proposes a
phased plan to drive a smooth evolution of Java client consumer
applications towards the next generation of the rebalance protocol

Here is the KIP:
https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/KAFKA/KIP-1274%3A+Deprecate+and+remove+support+for+Classic+rebalance+protocol+in+KafkaConsumer

Looking forward to hearing from you,

Thanks!
Lianet

**Finding**  
The log message that recommends switching from the classic rebalance protocol to the new consumer protocol is emitted when a Kafka consumer starts up and the configuration `group.protocol` is set to the value `classic`. In that case the client logs a warning at startup advising the user to switch to the new consumer protocol.  

**Evidence**  
- `event_id: mail:8e1a8d86c4f1e5741f91cb54` – “… we could still agree to a log line during start‑up recommending `classic` users to switch to the switch to `consumer` (after appropriate testing).”  
- `event_id: mail:2034d686308bfb1f60b2770e` – same wording.  
- `event_id: mail:c64a83d2563f7ab1569d318f` – same wording.  
- `event_id: mail:263b0239b98e36fe0c99fba8` – same wording.  
- `event_id: mail:ab91a8ee1efedccf40d3c5f8` – same wording.  
- `event_id: mail:4e7099123aab260e25a05d65` – same wording.  
- `event_id: mail:84430369388edaf5941313c9` – same wording.  
- `event_id: mail:8cafe5c1265af9d7eb31faa7` – same wording.  
- `event_id: mail:d6912ccc512d32df7a246110` – same wording.  

These messages all refer to the same discussion (KIP‑1274) and state that the log line will be emitted at startup for users configured with `group.protocol=classic`.

- event_id: mail:2034d686308bfb1f60b2770e | time: 2026-01-28T16:53:06.000000Z | body: About removing the config `group.protocol` with 6.0. I would advocate to do the removal, as originally proposed. If the config serves not purpose any longer (ie, has only one value), there seems to be no reason to keep it (this also help to reduce the number of config we have; which is a lot a not easy to navigate for users). Also, with AK 5.0, we plan to start to log a WARN when the config is used (for both values "classic" and "consumer"), and because "consumer" will be the default, we would expect users to not specifiy the config at all (also not with value "consumer" any longer), but to rely on the default.
